title: String Operations and Input
learningObjectives: Compare token extraction and whole-line input.
Use getline to capture spaces in text.
Handle leftover newline after formatted extraction.
Check stream state and validate user input.

understand.concept: Text input and operations include token extraction, getline, concatenation, comparison and searching. cin stops at whitespace; getline reads spaces.
understand.whyItMatters: Text processing is common in interactive applications.
understand.explain: Choose the input method, handle leftover newlines and check npos from searches.

examples.title: Check empty
examples.explanation: empty checks whether the string contains no characters.

examples.title: Search substring
examples.explanation: find returns a position or std::string::npos.

examples.title: Prepare getline after cin
examples.code: int age;\nif(std::cin>>age){std::cin.ignore(std::numeric_limits<std::streamsize>::max(),'\\n');std::string name;std::getline(std::cin,name);}\n// include <limits> for streamsize max
examples.explanation: Consume the leftover newline; include limits.

practise.guidedTask: For String Operations and Input, trace each example and record the collection type, size/capacity where relevant, valid index range, values before and after each operation, and what the code prints. Identify the key boundary case.
practise.independentTask: Write a C++ mini-task focused on String Operations and Input: use a small collection of values/text, perform at least three meaningful operations, and test normal, empty or boundary, and invalid-index/input cases. Explain your collection choice and expected output.
hints: Select the collection type and justify its size behavior.
Trace initialization and current element values.
Use bounds-aware access for potentially invalid indexes.
Prefer direct traversal when the index is not required.
Test empty, first, last and out-of-range scenarios.
